coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 10 units (domain root + 07.01..07.09), 57 markdown files, 1,171,738 bytes — exactly matching the expected 10 units / 57 files. Every file was read in full in the sandbox (large files in line-ranged chunks) and every unit ran the 3a implementer-simulation / 3b rubric / 3c devil's-advocate cycle. Scoring: dimensions 2 (Persona Specificity) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are N/A across every unit — personas are referenced from meta/personas.md and never redefined (07.03.01 Role Lens: 'Persona names from meta/personas.md — referenced, never redefined'), and no unit addresses competitors. Dimension 4 (Constraint Explicitness) is N/A at sub-domain level (budget/timeline/team/compliance axes live in meta/constraints.md) and applicable at the domain root. Per scoring.md ('Gaps found during Implementer Simulation are added directly to the punch list as ❌ items and also count toward the ambiguity score'), each finding is scored as its own checkpoint — blocking = 1.0, warning = 0.5 — added to the applicable rubric dimensions. All eight rubric dimensions themselves scored ✅ on their stated criteria in every unit (every folder has index + CX, every domain index has a populated Role Matrix, every feature file has a Role Lens, no Classification Gate violations, every open question carries an owner). FRESHNESS: nothing under .memory/wiki/specs/audits/ was read other than this run6 output path. One consequence: 07.01.03 and 07.01 D-03 cite '../../../audits/p01-production-stage-vocabulary-validation.md' as the gate that will fix the production-stage enum; that document was NOT consulted per the session-independence gate, and the P-01 deferral was therefore treated at face value as properly tracked ([OWNER], Q-01 → /create-prd) rather than audited. findings.claim: The inactivity period that ends a session is 12 hours in 07.06.01 and 6 hours in 07.06.02, stated flatly in both with no marker.
findings.evidence: 07.06.01-session-record-attendance.md:261 — '| D-18 | **Auto-close at 12h of inactivity**; **resume within 6h re-opens the same session**. Auto-close **defers** the prompt, never auto-confirms it |', and its edge case at line 152 — '| Producer **never closes**; session runs forever | Auto-closes after **12h with no activity** (no takes, no attendance changes, no bridge signal). A real session runs 10–14h *of activity*; 12h of silence is over.' Contradicted by 07.06.02-session-close-capture-prompt.md:146 — '| **Session runs past midnight / ten hours, 1am, exhausted** | The **design case, not the edge case**. A session is a continuous working block bounded by a wrap signal or **6 h of inactivity** (`02.02.01` D-12). |'
findings.forcedInvention: The session boundary determines the witness list, the capture grade, the attendance set and every credit derived from the session (07.06.01 D-08: the grade is 'inherited by every credit that comes out of it'). At 6h a dinner-and-evening tracking day splits into two sessions with two partial witness lists; at 12h it stays one. Both files are dated 2026-07-23 and neither defers the value.

findings.claim: The session resume/reopen model is unsatisfiable as written: the auto-closed-session resume case is arithmetically impossible against its own window, and the manual reopen window is 30 minutes in one file and 6 hours in the other.
findings.evidence: 07.06.01-session-record-attendance.md:153 — '| Session **resumes after a break** (dinner, a night\'s sleep) | Activity resuming within **6h** of the last activity **re-opens the same session**. Beyond 6h it is a new session.' and line 154 — '| Auto-closed session resumes at hour 13 | Reopens (**within the 6h window**) and un-closes. A `Deferred` prompt is withdrawn rather than fired twice.' Auto-close requires 12h of inactivity (D-18, line 261), so any resume after an auto-close is by construction more than 6h after the last activity and can never fall inside a window measured 'of the last activity'. Separately, 07.06.02-session-close-capture-prompt.md:148 — '| **Producer closes early by mistake** | Reopen within **30 minutes** un-closes the session and re-arms the moment. … **After 30 minutes it is a new session** (two sessions in a day is normal — `07.06.01`).' and its D-16 (line 227) — 'a reopen within 30 minutes re-arms it'.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must invent the origin the resume window is measured from (last activity, or the close event) and must reconcile 'after 30 minutes it is a new session' with 'beyond 6h it is a new session' for the 30-minute-to-6-hour band. Session identity is what the witness list and every derived credit hang off.

findings.claim: A readiness signal that two units describe as required of 07.08.03 — and describe as the loudest deficit the platform can carry — is absent from 07.08.03's input list and is tracked by no open question in either unit.
findings.evidence: 07.01.01-song-record-work-entity.md:258 — '**New signal from this pass**: a Song at `master approved` with **zero asserted recordings** is a finished record that is a rights object nowhere — the loudest completeness debt the platform can carry, and one 07.08.03 does not currently know to look for.' Restated at music-projects-collaboration-cx.md:199 — '**New signal `07.08.03` must learn to detect** (`07.01.01`→`07.08.03`): a Song at `master approved` with ZERO asserted recordings is a finished record that is a rights object nowhere — the thesis failing in the exact place it is meant to work, and the loudest completeness deficit possible.' 07.08.03-metadata-completeness-readiness-score.md:51-53 enumerates its inputs — 'credits captured or not (`07.06.02`), splits agreed or open (`07.06.02` D-03), sources declared (`07.08.04`, parent CX-02), QC results (parent CX-03), canonical set (`07.04.02`), ISRC/ISWC present' — with no such signal, and its open questions (Q-01 resolved, Q-02 resolved, Q-03 counter-attestation stall) do not carry it.
findings.forcedInvention: Neither statement of the obligation names an owner or a deferral target, and both use present-tense 'does not / must learn'. An implementer of 07.08.03 has no requirement to build the check; an implementer reading 07.01.01 expects the message it specifies at line 193 ('This song is mastered but isn\'t registered as a recording. Nothing you\'ve captured can be paid.') to exist.

findings.claim: The ratified v1 delivery for the Tier 1 contributor card is asserted without qualification to be the only surface that can meet its requirement, but it is unreachable for the unclaimed non-user contributor the roster calls the median case, and the verification item raised covers only a narrower caveat.
findings.evidence: 07.09.03-in-session-capture-surface.md:143 — '| D-08 | **The v1 delivery of the prompt is PWA web push + in-app** — both the Tier 1 contributor card and the Tier 2 Producer card … It is the **only v1-available surface** that can meet `07.06.02` D-09\'s Tier 1 requirement (≤ 5 s after the close signal, ungated)'. Restated at 07.06.02-session-close-capture-prompt.md:228 (D-17) and at music-projects-collaboration-index.md:103 (domain D-09). Tier 1 targets contributors: 07.06.02-session-close-capture-prompt.md:84 — '| 1 | **Contributors** | ≤ 5 s after the close signal, **ungated** | **≤ 2 interactions each** | The credit card'. But the contributor population is explicitly non-user: 07.03.01-contributor-roster-role-assignment.md:212 — 'The session drummer with no account is not an edge case — it is the median case for the next several years' and D-02 (line 244) — 'Roster entries may reference **unclaimed, non-user identities** (display name + optional contact channel)'. The only verification item raised is narrower: 07.09.03 Q-04 (line 153) — 'Does PWA web push actually deliver on iOS Safari without the PWA being installed to the home screen?'
findings.forcedInvention: A person who has never opened WeJammin has no push subscription and no installed PWA, so neither declared channel reaches them within the ≤ 5 s ungated Tier 1 budget. The tree does specify a non-user-addressable channel elsewhere (music-projects-collaboration-cx.md:97 — 'a NON-USER-addressable channel with its own global opt-out (D-14)'; 07.03.02 D-14/D-16), but no decision assigns it to the Tier 1 card, so the implementer must invent the channel and its latency for the majority of Tier 1 recipients.
